name: Plainfield
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Plainfield, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Plainfield, IL: Grinchmas on the Green, the Lions Club creche lighting, Santa wagon rides and Christmas trains near Plainfield.
lede: Plainfield starts Christmas in its historic downtown, where Santa and the Grinch light the big tree on the Village Green and the Lions Club lights a life size nativity scene on Lockport Street.
celebrates: Christmas in Plainfield centers on downtown and Lockport Street. The Plainfield Park District hosts Grinchmas on the Green at Village Green Park, with free hot cocoa and cookies under the pavilion, Santa and the Grinch arriving with help from the Plainfield Fire Protection District, a giant tree lighting and photos in a Whoville set up on the tennis court. Families and groups can buy their own tree to decorate for the park. The same evening, the Plainfield Area Public Library holds a free Handmade Holiday Market and the Lions Club lights its creche at Plymouth Congregational Church. The village also hosts Sparkle in the Park, a newer tree lighting at Settlers' Park.
lastyear: In 2025 Patch reported that Grinchmas on the Green, the library's Handmade Holiday Market with more than 60 vendors, and the Lions Club creche lighting were all planned for Small Business Saturday. Plymouth Congregational Church lists its 2025 creche lighting program as cancelled due to inclement weather. Grinchmas on the Green went ahead in early December, and Shaw Local photos show hundreds of families, kids playing in fresh snow, Santa arriving on a fire truck and a 7 year old helping Santa light the Christmas tree.
facts: The village says Plainfield is considered the oldest community in Will County, and its downtown is on the National Register of Historic Places. Plymouth Congregational Church on Lockport Street began building its meeting house in 1850 and is recognized as the oldest continually used church in Will County, Patch reported. The Plainfield Lions Club, founded in 1949, has set up its life size nativity scene at the church for 75 years as of 2026. When the program ends, everyone sings Silent Night outside and the scene stays lit all season.
trains: Plainfield has no Metra station of its own, so families drive to a neighboring stop. The Route 59 station in Aurora is on the BNSF Line, and the Joliet station at 90 E. Jefferson Street is served by the Rock Island and Heritage Corridor lines. Metra's Holiday Trains, specially decorated trains with holiday characters, run on several lines in December, including the BNSF and Rock Island. For a ride with Santa, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express.

Historic trolley rides along the Fox River in South Elgin, plus Santa's Trolley Express.
traditions: Santa and the Grinch arrive with the Plainfield Fire Protection District, light the giant Village Green tree and pose for photos in Whoville.
After carols and readings inside Plymouth Congregational Church, everyone sings Silent Night outdoors as the life size nativity is lit.
The Plainfield Area Public Library fills with vendors selling handmade gifts, treats and decor during the downtown festivities, and admission is free.
A Plainfield Park District wagon ride at Eaton Preserve takes families to visit Santa, with hot chocolate and cookies while you wait.
The park district serves breakfast at PARC with a goodie bag and a one on one visit with Santa, so bring your camera.
The village tree lighting at Settlers' Park adds student music, a holiday touch a truck, an ice carving demonstration and visits with Santa.
kidfact: At Grinchmas on the Green, Santa gets a ride from the Plainfield Fire Protection District, and last year he arrived on a fire truck. The nativity scene at Plymouth Congregational Church is life size, so the figures are about as tall as real people.
faq: What is Grinchmas on the Green in Plainfield?

Grinchmas on the Green is the Plainfield Park District's holiday kickoff at Village Green Park downtown. It starts with free hot cocoa and cookies under the pavilion, then Santa and the Grinch arrive with help from the Plainfield Fire Protection District and light the giant Christmas tree. Afterward, families can take photos with Santa and the Grinch in Whoville on the tennis court.
Where can we see the Plainfield creche?

The life size nativity scene stands outside Plymouth Congregational Church on Lockport Street. The Plainfield Lions Club lights it on the Saturday after Thanksgiving after a program of music, a singalong and readings of the Christmas story inside the church. The scene then stays lit for the rest of the holiday season, so families who miss the program can still see it.
Is there a Metra train to Plainfield?

No, Plainfield does not have its own Metra station. The nearest options are the Route 59 station in Aurora on the BNSF Line and the Joliet station on the Rock Island and Heritage Corridor lines. Both are a drive from Plainfield, and both lines carry Metra's specially decorated Holiday Trains in December, so a train ride can be part of a Christmas outing.

Several are. Grinchmas on the Green offers free hot cocoa and cookies, the library's Handmade Holiday Market has free admission, and the creche lighting has no ticket, though a freewill offering goes to the Plainfield Lions Club. Breakfast with Santa and Journey to the North Pole are run by the Plainfield Park District and need paid registration or tickets in advance.
What is Sparkle in the Park?

Sparkle in the Park is a holiday tree lighting hosted by the Village of Plainfield at Settlers' Park on Lockport Street. The village describes it as a new holiday tradition, with performances by local students and community groups, a tree lighting with the mayor and Santa, caroling, a holiday touch a truck, a live ice carving demonstration and seasonal treats.
